subject: Hosted readiness: p95/p99 runway & streaming concurrency follow-up
messages:
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@ordexa.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: alice.chen@ordexa.com, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted readiness: p95/p99 runway & streaming concurrency follow-up

Thanks Rafael and team — good call this morning, appreciate the crisp run through of Redwood's routing and fallback approach. A quick recap from our side and asks so we can scope the probe: 

Summary of ask
- Ordexa needs an apples-to-apples e2e p95/p99 comparison between our incumbent provider and Redwood hosted for our production traffic profile.
- We care about real-client-to-response latency (including network) for both non-streaming and streaming paths.
- Traffic pattern: attached CSV (ordexa_traffic_profile.csv) — short-turn streaming ~70% of requests, non-streaming completions ~30%; peak concurrency numbers included.

Clarifying questions / immediate asks
1) Can Redwood provide a short runbook for a 48-hour probe that will measure p95/p99 e2e (client -> Redwood -> client)? We want to verify streaming tail behavior and concurrent connections under synthetic load that mirrors the CSV.
2) What metrics/telemetry do you need from our side (SYN/ACKs, egress IPs, sample request IDs)?
3) Proposed acceptance thresholds: we think p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 650ms for the hosted candidate to be compelling vs incumbent — is that reachable? If not, provide expected runway and suggested mitigations (batching, KV caching, model variant).

Next steps: please send a proposed probe schedule + runbook and a list of any short-term config changes we need on our side. We also need an NDA/ack PDF for the live probe if there are any data handling specifics (attached: ordexa-sro-ack.pdf).

Thanks,
Tom Rivera
Head of AI, Ordexa
Tom.Rivera@ordexa.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@ordexa.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted readiness: p95/p99 runway & streaming concurrency follow-up

Tom — thanks for the clear recap and the traffic CSV. Short answers up front then a proposed probe runbook below.

TL;DR
- We can meet or beat your suggested acceptance for many common requests; typical hosted baselines we expect (given similar token lengths & model family): p95 ~ 160–230ms, p99 ~ 420–700ms. Exact numbers depend on sequence length distribution, client RTT, and streaming chunk size.
- We recommend a 48-hour side-by-side probe (incumbent vs Redwood hosted) with synthetic replay of the CSV-driven envelope and live sampling of production traffic.

Probe runbook (proposed) — 48-hour window
1) Prep (Day -2 to Day 0)
   - Ordexa: confirm stable test keys, open outbound IP ranges (we provide), and upload the traffic CSV to the Drive link you shared.
   - Redwood: pre-warm model variant, provide a canary endpoint + dedicated probe tokens, and a small probe harness container spec for your SREs.
2) Warm-up (0–2 hours)
   - Low-rate replay to populate caches and KV store where applicable.
3) Measurement windows (two 12-hour windows)
   - Window A: emulate 70/30 streaming/non-streaming mix, with the concurrency profile from CSV. Capture end-to-end timestamps (client send, first-byte, final-token, client receive).
   - Window B: spike & recovery tests (simulate 1.4× peak for 30 minutes) to observe tail risk and fallback behavior.
4) Telemetry & artifacts
   - Redwood will provide per-request latency buckets (p50/p90/p95/p99), token throughput, and server-side traces with request IDs.
   - From Ordexa we ask for: sample request IDs (10k), client-side timing (ms) for the same IDs, and network egress IPs to correlate.
5) Acceptance criteria (preliminary)
   - Host candidate must demonstrate either: (a) p95 within 1.15× incumbent and p99 within 1.3× while offering cost or throughput advantages, OR (b) absolute p95 <= 220ms and p99 <= 650ms for both streaming and non-streaming paths.

Configuration notes & mitigations
- If streaming tail exceeds p99 target we recommend: smaller chunk sizes, aggressive prefix caching, and bumping model variant to the quantized L2 for higher throughput (we detail tradeoffs later).

Deliverables we will send by end of day: canary endpoint, probe harness container spec, list of Redwood probe IPs, and a short template for request-ID correlation.

Attachments: referencing your ordexa_traffic_profile.csv and ordexa-sro-ack.pdf.

I'll post a calendar invite with a tentative run window tomorrow — are you available to start the probe on Tue 2028-03-06?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@ordexa.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: alice.chen@ordexa.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 03 Mar 2028 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted readiness: p95/p99 runway & streaming concurrency follow-up

Thanks Rafael — that runbook looks good. Quick clarifications from SRE side (Alice copied):
- Traffic CSV: peak concurrency in csv is 220 concurrent connections; sustained 110 qps during business hours.
- Streaming details: 70% short-turn streaming — average 12 tokens per response, chunks sent every 40–60ms by the client.
- We can provide client-side timing logs for sample request IDs; will produce a 10k sample set ahead of the probe.

Tue 2028-03-06 works for kickoff; prefer the 8am PST slot. We'll restore network access for your probe IPs and upload the confirmed CSV to the Drive folder by EOD Mon.

One more ask: who will be the Redwood on-call for the spike window (to discuss live fallbacks)?

Tom
Tom Rivera
Head of AI, Ordexa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@ordexa.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Mar 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted readiness: p95/p99 runway & streaming concurrency follow-up

Great — confirmed. Final runbook + schedule below and owners so everyone is clear.

Schedule
- Kickoff: Tue 2028-03-06 08:00 PST (30-minute sync) — Rafael and Camila to join live.
- Probe window: Tue 03/06 09:00 PST → Wed 03/07 09:00 PST (48 hours with two 12-hour measurement blocks and one spike test).

Owners & responsibilities
- Rafael Mendes (Redwood) — overall run conductor, will post mid-run notes and final summary, own canary endpoint config and correlation keys.
- Camila Reyes (Redwood) — telemetry lead, will share trace samples, per-token throughput, and p95/p99 buckets.
- Marissa Cole (Redwood) — stakeholder comms with Ordexa execs and procurement alignment if we need to extend trial.
- Alice Chen (Ordexa) — provide client timing logs and ensure probe tokens are whitelisted.
- Tom Rivera (Ordexa) — decision owner for acceptance thresholds and comms with product.

Acceptance checklist to sign off after run
- Correlated sample (10k IDs) uploaded and matched between client & Redwood logs.
- p95 & p99 tables for streaming and non-streaming.
- Cost per 10k requests comparison vs incumbent + recommended optimizations.
- Post-run call scheduled within 48 hours of probe end to review artifacts.

Links & artifacts (will populate prior to kickoff)
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4892
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcExample

Attachments: ordexa_traffic_profile.csv, ordexa-sro-ack.pdf (ack received).

If anything changes on your side overnight, ping me on Slack or reply here. We'll send the calendar invites and the probe harness container spec first thing tomorrow.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
